note.question: How should a franchisor or service principal combine pay, termination, prices, and monitoring when an agent can both underreport offline sales and secretly reduce effort?
note.overview: This is a dynamic principal-agent mechanism-design problem with two hidden actions: effort and truthful reporting of offline arrivals. The principal commits to compensation and termination, and extensions add dynamic pricing or monitoring; the paper derives incentive-compatible optimal contracts.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: At time zero the principal commits to a history-dependent contract. Over an infinite horizon the agent privately chooses effort and observes both arrival streams, reports the unobservable stream, and receives payments contingent on public and reported histories. The principal can terminate at a stopping time; extensions let the principal also change channel prices or activate monitoring dynamically. Which IC constraint binds depends on the relative severity of cash diversion and shirking.
